crime: Every evening by the lounge fire, one girl alters the others' dresses with pins and shears. She leaves every old stain in. "A stain is where a dress has lived," she says.

{WITCH_NAME} hands her the pins each night. The tailor is the only girl she lets stand that close, and the only one she never lets fit her. Before anyone can look at her, she runs a palm down her clothes and skin, and every crease and stain is gone, so no one looks long enough to find anything.

At nine, the prisoners leave their rumpled dresses on the sofa for pressing and go. {WITCH_NAME} stays for her first fitting. At five past, the tailor pins her dress, unpins it, pins it again, then takes the pins out. "Something's off. It isn't the dress. Come back another night."
{WITCH_NAME}'s mother used to change her clothes again and again before every outing, saying something wasn't right, and then leave her at home.

At eight past nine, {WITCH_NAME} drives the shears into the tailor's chest. At ten past, she wipes the blood from herself with her palm, passes it over every rumpled dress until each lies smooth as if pressed, and hangs them up. She sets the flatiron heating in the fireplace coals. At a quarter past, she joins the game at the pool table in the recreation room, spotless.
At ten to ten, the prisoners find the tailor dead, every dress pressed and the iron hot. She must have kept pressing for half an hour after {WITCH_NAME} left, they decide.

In the trial court, one prisoner looks at her pressed dress and finds it like new: the old stain the tailor left in it is gone. An iron lifts no stain. The prisoners realize it was {WITCH_NAME}'s palm that smoothed those dresses, after the tailor was already dead.
fields.epitaph: Of all the girls in that mansion, she killed the only one who never counted a mark against anyone.
execution: A giant copy of her spotless dress hangs from the execution stand, giant needles threaded along its open side seams. She hangs inside it by the shoulders. The needles begin stitching the seams shut, and with every pull the bodice draws tighter around her ribs. Each time a seam is finished, the needles unpick it and sew it again, tighter, as if something is still not right. At last she hangs still, the dress fitted without a single crease.

magic.name: Good as New
magic.text: One pass of her palm wipes away any scar, stain, scratch or crease.
